whyalla-1.name: Whyalla Maritime Museum
whyalla-1.bio: Whyalla's naval museum, home to HMAS Whyalla, the first modern warship built in South Australia.

notes.pin: Lincoln Highway, entry via Whyalla Visitor Centre; HMAS Whyalla on dry land beside it
notes.cost: Adult $19 (concession $16, child $13) from eyrepeninsula.com listing; admission includes guided HMAS Whyalla tour

whyalla-2.name: Point Lowly Lighthouse
whyalla-2.bio: The 1883 lighthouse on Point Lowly, built after reports of shipping dangers, overlooks the cuttlefish waters.

notes.pin: 42 Lighthouse Drive, Point Lowly; Wikipedia coords provisional (-32.99975,137.78563889)

whyalla-2.ticket_note: No single steward site found; Whyalla council tourism page only (whyalla.com), not a page for the lighthouse

whyalla-3.name: Giant Australian Cuttlefish Aggregation
whyalla-3.bio: Giant Australian cuttlefish gather in their tens of thousands to spawn off Whyalla each May to August.

notes.pin: Viewing/snorkel sites are in False Bay and Point Lowly waters; use the Point Lowly/Stony Point shore access, not the lighthouse pin
notes.cost: Free to snorkel or dive with own gear; guided tours and gear hire are paid and vary by operator, so no price stored

whyalla-4.name: Hummock Hill Lookout
whyalla-4.bio: A lookout over Whyalla and Spencer Gulf built into old World War Two gun emplacements.

notes.pin: Queen Elizabeth II Drive; pin on the hill's lookout, not the beach below

whyalla-4.ticket_note: Council-run open lookout, no single official page verified

whyalla-5.name: Whyalla Jetty
whyalla-5.bio: A 315 m circular jetty on the Whyalla foreshore for walking and fishing, lit all night.
whyalla-5.ticket_note: Open public structure; no dedicated official page verified

whyalla-6.name: Whyalla Foreshore
whyalla-6.bio: Whyalla's Spencer Gulf foreshore and marina, with a beach and dolphins often seen in the bay.

notes.pin: 1 Buttlingarra Way; beach/marina foreshore, keep 25 m+ from Whyalla Jetty pin (whyalla-5)

whyalla-6.ticket_note: Open public foreshore with no single steward page

whyalla-7.name: Whyalla Conservation Park
whyalla-7.bio: Wild Dog Hill rises from the plains north of Whyalla, with kangaroos and euros in the park.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point provisional; use the park's Wild Dog Hill picnic/access point off the Lincoln Highway, not the centroid

whyalla-8.name: Mount Laura Homestead Museum
whyalla-8.bio: National Trust museum in a 1914 homestead, with a steam locomotive and over 60 stationary engines.

notes.cost: Adult $10 (concession/under 16 $5); closed Saturdays and public holidays, open Sunday afternoon only (13:00-15:00)

whyalla-9.name: Freycinet Trail
whyalla-9.bio: A 12 km coastal route along Fitzgerald Bay to Point Lowly with a 4 km walking section.

notes.pin: Midpoint of the route along Fitzgerald Bay Road (hiking/cycling/driving trail, northern end of Fitzgerald Bay to Point Lowly); 4 km hiking section only is walkable

whyalla-9.ticket_note: Council trail; no verified dedicated page

whyalla-10.name: Gulf and Ranges Trail
whyalla-10.bio: A 4 km hiking and cycling loop at Crag Point with geology signs and views of the gulf and ranges.

notes.pin: Loop at Crag Point, Douglas Point; midpoint of the loop (halfway point may be off path, use trailhead if so)

whyalla-10.ticket_note: Council trail; no verified dedicated page

whyalla-11.name: Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum
whyalla-11.bio: Volunteer-run mining museum in the iron ore town of Iron Knob, on the Eyre Highway west of Port Augusta.

notes.pin: Iron Knob township (Wikivoyage -32.72,137.15 is the town); use the visitor centre building
notes.cost: Museum admission free, donations asked (town site); separate paid mine tours not included
notes.span: About 55 km from Whyalla, outside 75% of the 70 km span: destination span widened to 90 km

destination.name: Whyalla
destination.tagline: Steel city on Spencer Gulf, with a warship on land and winter cuttlefish
destination.description: Whyalla is South Australia's steel city on the upper Spencer Gulf, built around the iron ore from nearby Iron Knob. Its maritime museum holds HMAS Whyalla, a corvette launched in 1941 that now sits two kilometres from the sea. Every winter tens of thousands of giant Australian cuttlefish gather to spawn off Point Lowly. The foreshore has a circular jetty, a marina and a beach.
whyVisit: Dive with spawning cuttlefish in winter
Tour a World War II warship

goodToKnow.title: Bring or hire dive gear
goodToKnow.detail: Cuttlefish are viewed by snorkel or dive from May to August. Bring a wetsuit or hire gear, and go with a buddy or a guided group.

goodToKnow.title: Ship tours only
goodToKnow.detail: HMAS Whyalla can be entered only on a guided tour, included in museum admission. Wear closed-in footwear.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Winter is the time to come, when giant cuttlefish spawn off Point Lowly and the days stay mild ({months}).
